If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $4$ parts: the arc of the quarter-circle for 
$x\in [-6,-4),$ the line segment for $x\in (-4,-1],$ the line segment for 
$x\in (-1,1],$ and the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in [1,5].$ 
Therefore, we write

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-4}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the
$x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-4).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle minus a quarter-circle of radius $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =(2)(2)-\frac{1}{4}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =4-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis,

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{-4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=\pi -4.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-4,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3+1)\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,5].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =bh+\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =1(4)+\frac{1}{2}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =4+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =\pi -4+3+4+4+2\pi  \\  & =7+3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
